sources.title: Croatian Encyclopaedia, Serbia, medieval history
sources.note: Povijest, paragraphs on early principalities, Nemanjic kings, the empire and successor lordships. Used for political sequence, not prehistoric ethnic attribution or modern territorial claims.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Studenica Monastery
sources.note: Brief synthesis and criteria ii and iv: quarry settlement, Church of the Virgin, paintings of 1208-1209 and buildings added across several centuries.

sources.title: Ksenija Borojevic, Nutrition and environment in medieval Serbia, 2005
sources.note: Abstract, Vegetation History and Archaeobotany 14, pages 453-464: twelfth- and thirteenth-century Ras deposits, cereals, weeds, bread and peach fragments. Claims are restricted to the accessible abstract.

sources.title: Zivaljevic, Markovic and Maksimovic, Fish consumption at Studenica, 2019
sources.note: Author-shared paper, Anthropozoologica 54(16), pages 179-201, abstract and discussion: fourteenth- and early fifteenth-century waste, freshwater fish, sturgeon and interpretations of supply and preservation.

sources.title: Radicevic and Cicovic, A new discovery of a seal-die of Prince Lazar, 2016
sources.note: Starinar 66, pages 161-171, abstract: Drenje buildings, three churches, seal-die in pit 2 and date 1373-1389. Market function and deposition in 1390 are hypotheses, not direct observations.

sources.title: National Museum of Serbia, Archaeological Collection of Late Middle Ages
sources.note: Collection description, embroidered epitrachelion from the Church of Saints Peter and Paul near Novi Pazar, attributed stylistically to the late fourteenth or early fifteenth century.

sources.title: UNESCO Memory of the World, Miroslav Gospel
sources.note: Inscription description: illuminated parchment, Italian and Byzantine artistic influences, evangelistary structure and Rascian orthography. Late twelfth century avoids false precision between catalogue dates.

sources.title: UNESCO Tentative Lists, Smederevo Fortress
sources.note: Serbia submission of 2010, Description: return of Belgrade, new capital, riverside plan and court construction in 1428-1430. Tentative listing is not World Heritage inscription.

sources.title: Museum of Smederevo, Smederevo Fortress
sources.note: Fortress account: construction, transport, shortage of local building stone, reused masonry, conquest in 1459 and continued occupation under Ottoman rule.
